newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian industry worried about lira ERM rate.
newsitem.headline: Italian industry worried about lira ERM rate.

text.p: Giorgio Fossa, president of employers' association Confindustria, said on Monday that Italian businessmen were worried that the lira had rejoined the Europe Union's currency grid at too strong a rate.
"We are worried by the 990 central parity rate," Fossa told a conference in the northeast town of Udine. "We will have to measure up to this new exchange rate," he added.

EU finance ministers and central bank governors agreed late on Sunday to allow the lira to rejoin the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM), which it crashed out of four years ago, at a central rate of 990 lira to the mark.
Italy had originally sought to enter at a rate no stronger than 1,000 lira to the mark.

But Italy's EU partners, fearful of the damage a weak lira could do to their trade and of encouraging a weak currency to qualify for the single European currency, rejected that request. -- 39 6 678 2505
